meta.title: Nicolás Amorosi, full-stack engineer
meta.description: Full-stack engineer (TypeScript, Next.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL). I build and modernize business systems end to end, from the legacy database to production. Remote from Argentina; English, Spanish, Italian.

hero.role: Full-stack engineer, remote from Entre Ríos, Argentina
hero.now: I build the software organizations run on, from the legacy database to production. Right now that means <libretto>Libretto</libretto>, the academic records system of a theological faculty in Florence, and <payables>the rewrite of a university’s accounts-payable system</payables> out of Progress 4GL.
hero.before: Before that I led the team behind the <hr>HR and admin platform</hr> of the Italian Adventist Church Union, in Rome. I also build <himnova>Himnova Live</himnova>, open-source projection software for churches.
hero.status: Open to a full-time remote role, or to contract work. I work in English, Spanish and Italian.
hero.note: Old databases spell my name <bytes>NicolÃ¡s</bytes>. Getting it right, twenty years of records at a time, is part of the job: <fix>this is how I fixed it for a faculty in Florence</fix>.

work.title: Selected work
work.note: Client code is private, so the case studies show problems, decisions and outcomes instead of code. The exception is Himnova Live, which is open source. I’m happy to walk through any of it in an interview.

about.title: About
about.p1: I studied at Universidad Adventista del Plata (Systems Analyst in 2022, Systems Engineer in 2024) and wrote my first production code there, upgrading the university’s Rails applications.
about.p2: In 2025 I moved to Rome to run IT and development at HopeMedia Italia, the media centre of the Italian Adventist Church Union. Since August 2026 I work remotely from Entre Ríos, Argentina, for clients in Italy and Argentina. I’m an Italian citizen.
about.p3: Off the clock I fly FPV drones and keep a repair log for each one, go running, self-host a home server, and I’m building an ESP32 rack that waters balcony plants on its own.

contact.title: Contact
contact.lead: Email is the quickest way to reach me.
contact.hours: Entre Ríos runs on UTC−3 all year, so my working day overlaps the European afternoon and the whole US East Coast day.

case.privacy: The code belongs to the client and stays private. Figures are illustrations with sample data; no real records appear on this page.
case.openSource: This project is open source: its code, issues and releases are public on GitHub. Figures are illustrations.

scopes.caption: One request for grades, answered for three people. The scope becomes a database filter; grades outside it never leave the server.

encoding.fffd: {count, plural, one {# replacement character. The gate refuses to write.} other {# replacement characters. The gate refuses to write.}}
encoding.silent: No replacement characters, but a character is gone
encoding.caption: The same bytes through three decoders. UTF-8 fails loudly, latin1 fails silently, Windows-1252 gets it right.

approval.caption: Built at submission time by walking up the hierarchy. Each step keeps a snapshot of its approver, so a reorganization never rewrites past approvals.
approval.effectNote: Approved absences become entries in the monthly report

archaeology.caption: From opaque sources to a map, then to a new database, without ever touching production.
archaeology.map: Map of tables, programs and history
archaeology.reconcileNote: Totals checked against the old system

projection.caption: The projection window only renders the last output it received, so it can always be rebuilt. Slides are never converted: the app reads each deck itself and the renderer draws it.
projection.controlNote: The operator queues songs, passages, slides
projection.mainNote: Owns state and SQLite; replays the last output
projection.screenNote: A pure function of the last output
